title: A boundary re-exec restarts the loop's --max-cycles budget and its wave index (every wave-21 summary said 'wave 0')
summary: When a lane ship moves HEAD past the running binary's build commit, the chain boundary refresh rebuilds and re-executes the loop with os.Args unchanged (chainReExecArgvFn). The new process starts its iteration counter at 0 with the original --max-cycles, so every wave after a ship is logged and signalled as 'wave 0' (wave 21 printed '[loop] wave 0: 2/2 lanes ok' at every close) and the operator's cycle budget restarts at each shipping wave; while ships keep landing the loop never reaches --max-cycles.
acceptance: The re-exec carries the batch's completed-iteration count (or the remaining budget) so the new process continues the same wave index and stops at the operator's --max-cycles.
A test re-execs through the chainReExecArgvFn seam after one completed wave and asserts the next wave's index is 1 and the remaining budget is max-1.
priority_rationale: wave 21 boundary 2026-09-28: the operator cannot tell waves apart in the log or the Signal Center, and --max-cycles is not a bound while ships land
consumed_by: console landing fix/loop-controls (2026-09-29): BUILT for the wave boundary. The breaker marker the wave-boundary refresh arms also records the pid and the completed-wave count in their own fields (loopchain.WithHandoff; pid, waves_done; syscall.Exec keeps the pid). runLoop takes it once at boot, before the chain/batch split (loopchain.TakeHandoff): honoured only for the same pid, a different build commit and an arm at most five minutes old; the run resumes at the completed-wave index with the remaining budget (a chained run's first batch only) and the record is consumed. No new flag or env var; a chain-boundary re-exec arms no handoff. Not covered: a chain-boundary re-exec still restarts the chain's own batch count and max_batches.
